Comments: Cross-border functionality exists regionally: Moov Money Burkina Faso supports transfers within UMOA countries; additionally BCEAO PI‑SPI platform is designed for interoperable instant operations across WAEMU. Comments: Burkina Faso launched government digital payment platform Faso Arzêka enabling citizens to pay taxes/fees and other administrative services via mobile app/USSD using mobile money, bank cards, and bank transfers, indicating active P2G payments.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No general mandatory data breach notification obligation identified in Burkina Faso personal data law summaries; DLA Piper notes no general obligation to notify data subjects in case of a security breach (only limited rectification notice in Art. 21).

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Burkina Faso participates in WAEMU payment infrastructures; BCEAO launched the Interoperable Instant Payment System Platform (PI‑SPI) for all WAEMU countries on 30 Sep 2025, after real-life tests started 5 Jun 2025, enabling interoperable instant transfers and payments 24/7 between banks, MFIs and e-money issuers; as of 2026 evidence indicates launch and gradual rollout rather than universal end-user saturation, so treated as partially deployed.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Global Findex 2021 shows 36% of adults in Burkina Faso have an account (financial institution or mobile money) per World Bank Open Data series; this suggests active digital financial account usage in the 20-49% band.
